t: PowerTrain test bench – Final-year project at Metacar Mobility Systems
d:
▶ **Open the interactive demo of the supervision interface**: https://medamindriss.wixsite.com/amin-driss-insa-lyon/interface-banc-powertrain

Final-year internship (March – September 2026) at Metacar Mobility Systems, a Lyon start-up developing the Kiwee, a nestable electric vehicle for car sharing.

Mission: design, build and commission a PowerTrain test bench in a **Back-to-Back** architecture to measure the efficiency of the vehicle's in-wheel motor.

What I did:
• Mechanical design in **SolidWorks**: welded frame validated by finite element analysis, safety cover, shaft line with rotary torque meter
• Electrical design: schematics and wiring of the power and control cabinet, safety chain
• Instrumentation: Hall-effect **current sensors** with an analog signal-conditioning circuit
• Embedded control: programming of two **ACTIA SPU 40-26** controllers communicating over **CAN bus**, two-mode strategy (torque-torque and speed-torque) with discrete **PID controllers**
• Supervision: interface developed in **Python** and then ported to **C++** (**Dear ImGui** / **ImPlot**): bench control, real-time plots, automatic torque-speed tests, power balance and efficiency, sensor readings, CAN message decoding from DBC files, works with a PEAK (PCAN) adapter or **METACAN**
• METACAN: design of a USB gateway to 4 independent CAN buses, based on an **ESP32** and 4 **MCP2515** controllers, with an OLED screen showing the state of each bus (Arduino/C++ firmware)
• Commissioning, test campaigns and analysis of the results

Result: the bench is operational, its operating envelope is characterised and next improvements are identified.

Tools: SolidWorks, ACTIA SPU 40-26, CAN bus (DBC, PCAN), C++ (Dear ImGui, ImPlot, CMake), Python, ESP32, MCP2515

t: Scale model of a convoy of nestable electric vehicles – INSA Lyon x Metacar research project
d:
Research and Innovation Project (2025 – 2026) carried out at INSA Lyon with Metacar, around the **Kiwee** concept: electric vehicles that nest into each other like supermarket trolleys so that one operator can move them as a convoy.

Objective: design and control a **working 1/10 scale model** able to drive as a convoy and to nest mechanically.

What I did:
• Mechanical design in **SolidWorks** and **3D printing**: front, rear and middle chassis matching the geometry and mass distribution of the real vehicle, pivot joint at ±37°
• Electronics: decentralised architecture based on **Arduino Nano ESP32** boards, custom **PCB**, encoders, pivot sensor and inertial measurement unit
• Communication: control from a PC over Wi-Fi (UDP) with a gamepad, then relay of the commands from one vehicle to the next over a serial link
• Control: modelling in **Simulink**, **PID** speed control with digital filtering, wheel synchronisation, electronic differential in turns and **convoy stabilisation**

Result: convoy stability, path following and control robustness validated by tests.

Tools: SolidWorks, 3D printing, ESP32, PCB design, C++, Python, MATLAB/Simulink

t: COPR projects at INSA Lyon: INSA Racing Team battery cart and ChirBaby simulator
d:
At INSA Lyon, COPR projects (team projects of the Mechanical Engineering department) give a team of engineering students a real need to work on, from needs analysis to a sized solution.

1. Battery cart for the **INSA Racing Team** (COPR 4, 2025)
Team of six students, for INSA's **Formula Student** team. The rules require a dedicated cart to remove, move and have the battery of the electric car inspected.
• **Functional analysis**: stakeholders, life phases, ranking of functions (fit with the battery, braking, safety, fastening, protection against vibrations).
• Search for solutions: split into 7 subsystems and selection with the **TOPSIS** method.
• Chosen solution: welded square steel tube frame, 4 solid wheels (2 swivel wheels at the front), brake always engaged on the rear wheels by spring-loaded pads and released with bicycle brake levers, metal firewall, anti-vibration mounts and the same fastening as on the car.
• **SolidWorks** CAD, cost estimate (about €208 excl. VAT for a €200 budget) and finite element checks: tray under a 90 kg battery (from 4 to 16 mounts to stay below the yield strength of S235 steel) and buckling of the legs.
• Eco-design (NF E 01-005) and project management: charter, risks, schedule.

2. **ChirBaby 2.0** newborn simulator – vital signs module (COPR S2, June 2025)
Team of seven students, for Dr Frédérick Hameury of the Hospices Civils de Lyon. ChirBaby is a newborn manikin on which surgeons train for oesophageal atresia surgery. Our team had to make its vital signs visible and let the anaesthetist listen to it.
• Respiratory simulator in **Python**: pressure, volume, flow and exhaled CO2 curves, adjustable free mode (volume or pressure control) and critical scenarios such as pneumothorax.
• Link with the team that animates the organs: breathing rate and the pneumothorax and curarisation modes are sent to an Arduino board.
• My role, in the Arduino and Auscultation teams: circuit of **force sensors** (**FSR**) connected to an **Arduino Nano ESP32** that talks to the computer over Wi-Fi, and an auscultation interface with 6 lung zones and 2 heart zones. Pressing a sensor plays the matching breathing sound, taken from a bank of digital stethoscope recordings. An "auscultation" mode and an "operation" mode prevent the sensors from triggering during surgery.

Tools: SolidWorks, Python, Arduino, functional analysis, TOPSIS, finite element analysis, project management.

t: Combat and all-terrain robots – ENIS Electrical Club (2022 – 2024)
d:
In the Electrical Club of ENIS (Sfax), I took part in designing robots: team member from 2022 to 2023, then **project leader** from 2023 to 2024.

What I did:
• Design and build of **combat robots** and **all-terrain robots**, from mechanics to control.
• Design and simulation of electronic circuits in **Proteus**: **Arduino**-based boards, **transistor and relay** power stages to drive the motors.
• Integration, wiring and testing of the robots.
• As project leader: task allocation, schedule follow-up and team coordination.
• Organisation of the **ENISROBOT 6.0** robotics event.

Tools: Arduino (C/C++), Proteus, power electronics (transistors, relays), mechanical design.

d:
End-of-year project at ENIS (2024), carried out in a team of three for the company Jufré: design and build an **automatic machine** that washes fruit before pressing, instead of washing it by hand.

What we did:
• Needs analysis and **specifications**: throughput, budget and food hygiene.
• Choice of solutions with a decision matrix: water agitation by blowers, rinsing by spray nozzles and emptying by tilting the tank with a **pneumatic** cylinder.
• Sizing of the **stainless steel** tank, the cylinder and the frame, and study of the **hydraulic circuit**.
• Complete design in **SolidWorks**, with costs kept within the set **budget**.
• **Manufacturing**, **assembly and a washing test** on a batch of lemons.
det: Mechanical design · SolidWorks CAD · Sizing · Pneumatics and hydraulics · Manufacturing

t: Industrial visits to MISFAT and CAVEO – ENIS (2024)
d:
Industrial visits made in 2024 with ENIS (National Engineering School of Sfax) to two Tunisian companies: **MISFAT**, a maker of automotive filters, and **CAVEO**.

What I saw:
• Mass **production lines**: making and assembling filters, and making leaf springs.
• Quality control stations, such as the filter leak test.
• How workstations are organised: **work instructions** and quality sheets posted at each station, production flow and safety.

These visits helped me link my manufacturing and quality courses to the reality of industrial production.
det: Mass production · Quality control · Industrial organisation
im: Industrial visit: overview of a production workshop

t: Refurbishment of a cold gold rolling mill (2024)
d:
Refurbishment, done on my own, of a cold gold rolling mill used in jewellery making (April 2024).

• **Diagnosis of the machine**, which was out of service, and of its electrical cabinet.
• Rework and improvement of the **power section**: **transformers**, **contactors**, **terminal blocks** and complete rewiring of the panel.
• Recommissioning and testing of the machine.
• 3D model of the rolling mill (central column and two rolling heads) to present the machine.
